name: Eiffel Tower
description: Paris’s iron lattice tower rises over the Champ de Mars. Evening lights sparkle on the hour after dusk.

name: Louvre Museum
description: A former palace turned vast museum around I. M. Pei’s glass pyramid. Reserve timed entry for popular wings.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel
description: An abbey-crowned island rises from tidal flats. Causeway access depends on the tide schedule.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
description: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité is undergoing restoration after the 2019 fire; façades remain a landmark.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: Louis XIV’s château opens onto formal gardens and the Hall of Mirrors. Arrive early for shorter queues.

name: Banks of the Seine
description: UNESCO-listed riverbanks link bridges, bookstalls and evening walks through central Paris.

name: Valensole plateau
description: Lavender fields colour Provençal plateaus in summer. Cycle tracks and farm stands line the back roads.

name: Annecy old town
description: Canals and pastel houses sit beside an Alpine lake. The waterfront path is busy in warm months.

name: Calanques National Park
description: Limestone inlets drop into clear water east of Marseille. Trailheads fill early on sunny weekends.

name: Pont du Gard
description: A three-tier Roman aqueduct spans the Gardon. Walkways and a museum explain the water system.

name: Marché Bastille
description: A large open-air market along Boulevard Richard-Lenoir sells produce, cheese and rotisserie.

name: Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
description: Lyon’s celebrated covered food hall gathers cheese, oysters and bouchon-style counters.

name: Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen
description: Paris’s vast flea-market district includes cafés and snack stands among antique alleys.

name: Marché Forville
description: A Provençal market in Cannes sells flowers, olives and ready-to-eat Provençal dishes.

name: Marché des Capucins
description: Bordeaux’s lively market hall is known for oysters, canelés and south-west produce.

name: Fête des Lumières
description: Lyon’s December light festival projects art onto façades across the Presqu’île and hills.
